title: Multimodal alignment improves generalizability of genomic biomarker prediction in computational pathology
abstract: Computational pathology models that use digitized histopathology whole-slide images have the potential to become a cost-effective and scalable alternative to molecular assays for the prediction of genomic biomarkers, a key task in precision oncology. However, as new genomic biomarkers are discovered or quantified, large, labeled datasets must be prospectively collected to train new models. To address this challenge, we developed multimodal alignment for biomarker learning and generalization (MARBLE), a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that integrates structured biomarker knowledge into representation learning of histopathology images. MARBLE aligns histopathology-derived representations with representations of genomic biomarkers generated by a large language model (LLM) and a protein language model (PLM). This biologically informed alignment enables data-efficient generalization to novel, out-of-distribution biomarkers. Using the MSK-IMPACT cohort of over 40,000 patients across multiple biomarker panel versions, we design experiments grounded in real-world data to demonstrate the value of our proposed approach.

title: Triết học về hình thức biểu hiện của J.G. Fichte và vấn đề bản quyền trong kỷ nguyên trí tuệ nhân tạo
authors: PGS.TS. Trần Văn Hải / Phó Vũ Thục Hiền
abstract: Bài viết nghiên cứu khả năng vận dụng luận điểm “hình thức biểu hiện” của Fichte - hạt nhân của học thuyết nhân cách - vào việc giải quyết các thách thức của quyền tác giả trong kỷ nguyên trí tuệ nhân tạo. Theo Fichte, hình thức biểu hiện là dấu ấn độc nhất, là sự mở rộng nhân cách của một chủ thể tự ý thức (con người) và là nguyên tắc bảo hộ tối cao quyền tác giả, tư tưởng này đã trở thành nguyên tắc phân đôi ý tưởng - hình thức biểu hiện (Idea–Expression Dichotomy) trong pháp luật về quyền tác giả hiện đại. Đối diện với tác phẩm có sự hỗ trợ của trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI), bài viết vận dụng luận điểm của Fichte để giải mã bản chất của câu lệnh trong trường hợp là ý tưởng và trong trường hợp là hình thức biểu hiện. Từ đó, đề xuất tiêu chuẩn về mức độ đóng góp của con người trong hình thức biểu hiện làm cơ sở xác định tính nguyên gốc để bảo hộ quyền tác giả. Kết luận khẳng định, dù công nghệ thay đổi, tác phẩm có thể được hình thành theo các cách khác nhau, nhưng tư tưởng của Fichte vẫn là nguyên tắc tối thượng để bảo hộ quyền tác giả trong kỷ nguyên AI.

title: 面向换流变压器故障溯源的可解释知识图谱推理方法
abstract: 换流变压器是高压直流输电系统的关键设备，其故障演化过程具有非线性和强耦合特征。针对运维文本数据利用不足和诊断过程缺乏可解释性的问题，提出一种可解释知识图谱推理方法（IKGR）。首先，采用ALBERT-BiLSTM-CRF从检修记录和故障报告等非结构化文本中抽取实体，并依据图谱模式层和物理因果约束组织关系三元组，构建换流变压器故障溯源知识图谱。其次，设计双智能体强化学习推理模型，引入软奖励机制，并利用短期同策略轨迹缓冲区同步更新双智能体参数，实现多跳故障溯源。实验结果表明， IKGR的根因排序指标Hits@10达到94.8%，并可生成包含设备部件、故障状态、保护动作和试验方法的推理路径，为换流变压器故障处置和运维决策提供路径级解释。

title: Trusted grounded retrieval-augmented generation for journalism
abstract: The rapid evolution of generative artificial intelligence (AI) presents significant evaluation challenges. As large language models are increasingly exposed to misinformation, synthetic content, and imperfect web-scale training data, grounding model outputs in trusted, verifiable contexts has become essential. Conventional benchmarking based on static datasets does not adequately capture factual grounding and contextual relevance in operational settings. To address these limitations, the European Broadcasting Union adopted a use-case-driven framework focused on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for public service media (PSM). The paper examines how curated, high-quality PSM archives can anchor model behaviour and improve factual reliability. Four contributions are presented. First, the paper describes a practical RAG architecture covering query formulation, document chunking, vector retrieval, reranking, and contextual generation, with attention to reranking strategies that constrain model improvisation. Second, it proposes a multilayered evaluation framework combining information retrieval metrics, factual consistency checks, answer coverage assessment, and expert human judgement. Third, it introduces a smart writing assistant that uses trusted context to support journalistic ideation and drafting while preserving full editorial control. Finally, it explores bounded agentic workflows in which an additional layer intervenes only when retrieval quality is insufficient. Together, these components show how trusted corpora, transparent evaluation, and controlled automation can improve reliability while keeping journalists in command of the editorial process. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.

title: Using counterfactual explanations to enable prescriptive analytics in educational data mining projects
abstract: As machine learning (ML) models are increasingly used to support decision making in higher education, there is a growing need to move beyond accurate prediction toward explanations that enable meaningful intervention. This paper examines counterfactual explanations (CFEs) as prescriptive complements to risk prediction in educational data analytics. While predictive models can flag students at risk, their practical value is limited without actionable guidance. CFEs address this need by proposing small, feasible changes that may shift a prediction from at-risk to not at-risk. Three approaches are compared on the Student Insomnia and Educational Outcomes (SIEO) dataset using a LightGBM classifier as the predictive backbone: DiCE (genetic search), the method of Wachter et al. (optimisation with proximity penalties), and a FACE-lite approximation that follows manifold-constrained paths via nearest-neighbour graphs. Demographic variables (eg gender, year of study) are treated as immutable; behavioural and psychological features (eg sleep duration, fatigue, stress) are allowed to vary. Counterfactual quality is assessed by validity, proximity, sparsity, and plausibility. Results indicate that improving sleep, reducing fatigue, and lowering stress frequently appear as pathways for altering model outputs. The comparison suggests distinct trade-offs: DiCE tends to increase diversity with occasional plausibility concerns; Wachter emphasises minimal changes with more repetitive adjustments; FACE-lite balances plausibility with structural constraints. Taken together, these findings point to CFEs as a practical complement to predictive analytics, offering individualised recommendations that can inform advising and student support. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.

title: CarePal: Multilingual Contradiction-Aware Conversational System for Structured Symptom intake
abstract: CarePal is a conversational intake system designed to collect symptom histories in settings where linguistic diversity, inconsistent narratives, and limited clinical time reduce the quality of pre-diagnosis information.The system integrates adaptive question generation, multilingual alignment, and the detection of contradictions through three core algorithmic components: (1) an Adaptive Question Generation Engine that dynamically constructs symptom inquiries based on patient responses, (2) a Multilingual Semantic Alignment Module that preserves meaning across Hindi, Bengali, and English, and (3) a Contradiction Detection and Resolution Framework that identifies and resolves inconsistencies in patient narratives.This paper outlines the architecture, training process, hyperparameter tuning, detailed algorithm specifications, and evaluation using quantitative metrics on 1,260 synthetic dialogues, providing simulation-based evidence of system performance, alongside usability data from a survey-based study with 26 participants.We hypothesized that CarePal would increase symptom-history completeness and internal consistency compared with a template-based intake system.

title: Qubits of a Feather, Flawed Together: A Critical Survey Review of Quantum Computing Architectures Compared
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Quantum Computing Architectures Compared in the context of Physics. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of quantum computing and qubits as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Physics.

title: Based on Formal Semantics-Based Robot Control Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to robot control learning based on formal semantics. Traditional robot control methods often rely on trial-and-error learning or hand-crafted rules, which can be inefficient and unreliable, particularly in complex and uncertain environments. Our approach leverages formal semantics to represent robot actions and environmental states precisely, enabling more accurate and robust control learning. We define a framework where robot actions and the corresponding environment states are formalized as mathematical models. Using formal semantics, we then perform control learning tasks such as planning, reasoning, and decision-making. The core claim is that this formalized approach significantly improves the accuracy and reliability of robot control strategies. We detail the underlying mathematical framework, focusing on how formal semantics addresses the challenges inherent in traditional control methods. This work demonstrates the potential of formal semantics to provide a solid foundation for intelligent robot control, paving the way for more adaptable and dependable robotic systems. ---

title: Privacy-Preserving Computation Protocols Based on Quantum Coherence Degradation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum coherence degradation for designing more secure privacy-preserving computation protocols. The core concept hinges on manipulating the rate of quantum decoherence to safeguard user data during quantum computation, thereby mitigating the risks of eavesdropping and attacks. We explore theoretical frameworks and propose protocol designs that explicitly incorporate and control decoherence, offering a novel approach to quantum privacy. The primary contribution lies in demonstrating how controlled decoherence can be a robust mechanism for data protection in quantum settings, providing a foundation for future research and development in this area. The proposed protocols aim to achieve a balance between computational efficiency and privacy preservation, a critical challenge in the field of quantum privacy. Further investigation and optimization are needed to translate these theoretical concepts into practical implementations.

title: ## The Epauletted Bat Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Aerial Maneuvers
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Epauletted Bat Metaheuristic (EBM), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Epauletted Bat ( *Rhinolophus clivosus*). The bat's unique aerial maneuver – the epauletted flight – where bats adjust their flight direction and speed based on local food source density – provides a powerful analogy for optimization problems. The EBM algorithm utilizes a population of bats, each representing a potential solution. Bats iteratively adjust their position and velocity based on a modified version of the bat's echolocation strategy, incorporating a local food source density estimation mechanism. This mechanism, based on the mean of the best solutions in the current population, provides a robust and adaptive guide for bats to converge towards optimal solutions. The algorithm's parameters are carefully tuned to balance exploration and exploitation, leading to effective performance across a range of benchmark functions. Experimental results demonstrate the EBM's competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) in solving continuous optimization problems. The EBM's simplicity and effectiveness make it a promising alternative for various real-world optimization challenges.

title: Bushveld Gerbil: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bushveld Gerbil Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Bushveld Gerbil (BG), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Allactopharynx albifrons*, commonly known as the Bushveld Gerbil. The algorithm leverages the gerbil's efficient exploration and exploitation strategies within a complex environment, specifically focusing on their burrowing and food-searching patterns. BG employs a combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and a simulated annealing (SA) approach, incorporating a novel 'burrowing' mechanism to enhance exploration and a 'food preference' weighting system to prioritize promising solutions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities. Specifically, the algorithm is designed to efficiently navigate a search space while avoiding premature convergence, mimicking the gerbil's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on environmental feedback. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of the search radius and the implementation of a local search strategy mirroring the gerbil's tendency to revisit promising areas. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance, highlighting its potential for solving complex optimization challenges.

title: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Inference with Superposition
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Bayesian inference that draws inspiration from the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and decoherence. Traditional Bayesian inference often struggles with exploring the vast and complex inference landscape, leading to slow convergence and potential inaccuracies. Our method utilizes a quantum-inspired representation of probability distributions as quantum states, enabling the simultaneous consideration of multiple hypotheses within a superposition. Controlled decoherence protocols are then employed to guide the inference process, effectively selecting the most probable hypothesis while minimizing computational cost. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and mathematical formulations, that this approach can dramatically improve the exploration of the inference landscape, resulting in faster convergence and enhanced accuracy compared to conventional Bayesian methods. The core of this work lies in the mapping of Bayesian model parameters to quantum states and the implementation of controlled decoherence, offering a fundamentally new perspective on probabilistic reasoning. This research aims to provide a framework for tackling complex Bayesian problems efficiently and effectively, potentially unlocking new possibilities in various fields, including machine learning, statistics, and scientific discovery.

title: Brown's Pademelon: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Brown's Pademelon's Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, Brown's Pademelon (BP), inspired by the foraging behavior of Brown's Pademelons, a small macropod native to Australia. These animals exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between short bursts of intense searching and periods of relaxed observation. BP leverages this behavior to create a robust and efficient optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a 'search burst' phase with adaptive step size, a 'relaxed observation' phase with probabilistic acceptance, and a novel 'memory consolidation' technique. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BP through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that BP outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, including Genetic Algorithms (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA), particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multimodal solutions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. This work provides a valuable addition to the field of metaheuristic optimization and offers a promising approach for tackling challenging real-world problems.

title: Cognitive Graph Embeddings for Knowledge Representation
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly used for various applications, including question answering, recommendation systems, and semantic search. However, traditional graph embedding methods often struggle to effectively represent the complex, hierarchical, and contextual relationships inherent in KGs. This paper introduces Cognitive Graph Embeddings (CGEs), a novel approach that integrates cognitive biases and reasoning heuristics into the graph embedding process. CGEs employ a multi-layer architecture, combining established graph embedding techniques with layers inspired by human cognitive models – specifically, associative memory and attention mechanisms. This allows the model to capture richer representations that more closely align with how humans understand and retrieve knowledge. We demonstrate that CGEs outperform standard graph embeddings on several benchmark datasets, highlighting the potential of incorporating cognitive principles into KG representation.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on high-dimensional space logic, designed to automatically discover optimal solutions and leverage structural properties to effectively address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's key innovation lies in its ability to intelligently adapt to the inherent structure of the problem space, resulting in improved performance compared to existing techniques. This research explores the potential of high-dimensional space logic for solving complex optimization challenges across diverse fields, including machine learning, robotics, and data analysis. title: Self-Correcting Code via Formal Language Theory and Compiler Transformations
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to software development centered around a self-correcting compiler. The core idea is to leverage formal language theory and sophisticated compiler transformations to automatically detect and rectify errors within source code. Traditional static analysis techniques often struggle with the nuances of semantic errors and require extensive manual intervention. This work introduces a compiler architecture that utilizes formal language models to perform a deep semantic analysis of the code, identifying violations of the programming language's rules. Upon detection, the compiler automatically applies targeted transformations to resolve these errors, resulting in a corrected version of the source code. This approach offers the potential for significant improvements in software quality, developer productivity, and reduced debugging time. The key innovation lies in the integration of formal language models – a departure from conventional static analysis – allowing for a more precise and comprehensive understanding of code semantics. The proposed system aims to move towards a future where software development is more robust and less reliant on manual error correction.

title: Neural Symbolic Adaptive Generation Model (NSAGM)
abstract: This paper introduces the Neural Symbolic Adaptive Generation Model (NSAGM), a novel approach to generative modeling that addresses the challenges of semantic consistency, knowledge completeness, and adaptability in generated content. The core idea is to integrate symbolic reasoning within a generative model framework. NSAGM leverages a combination of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to achieve this. A symbolic knowledge graph is constructed using a GNN, representing relationships between input and latent variables. The VAE learns a probability distribution within the latent space. During generation, the GNN guides the VAE to produce latent vectors consistent with the knowledge graph, ensuring semantic coherence and factual accuracy. An adaptive module dynamically adjusts the knowledge graph and GNN parameters based on feedback, such as human preferences or external knowledge updates. The key innovation lies in the dynamic, context-aware adaptation of the knowledge graph, enabling simultaneous optimization of semantic consistency and knowledge completeness. This approach, coupled with the integration of GNNs and VAEs for encoding symbolic knowledge in the latent space, represents a significant advancement over existing generative models.

title: PSouffle: Scaling Exact Probabilistic Logic Inference for Program Analysis
abstract: Probabilistic extensions of logic programming languages, such as ProbLog, allow users to annotate facts and rules with probabilities and have been useful in domains such as quantitative program analysis. However, exact inference for such programs often fails to scale to program-analysis workloads, where large derivation graphs and many probabilistic variables make decision-diagram construction prohibitively expensive. We present PSouffl´e, an exact and scalable inference toolchain built on Souffl´e for probabilistic Datalog programs. Its key contribution is a semantics-preserving rewriting of Datalog derivation graphs: by exploiting conditional independence in local derivation structures, PSouffl´e replaces these structures with smaller equivalent representations, thereby reducing the number of probabilistic variables exposed to decision-diagram construction. We evaluate PSouffl´e on 50 benchmarks from power side-channel analysis, taint analysis, and disassembly analysis. PSouffl´e completes every benchmark within the 30-minute timeout, while three state-of-the-art baseline solvers, ProbLog2, vProbLog, and Scallop, complete only 12%, 54%, and 32%, respectively. On benchmarks completed by all tools, PSouffl´e achieves average speedups of 219× over ProbLog2, 119× over vProbLog, and 18× over Scallop.

title: 67 Foundation Model Embeddings Identify Spatial Restructuring Associated with Immunotherapy Treatment Derived from Hemoxylin and Eosin Images
abstract: Abstract Background Patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) who receive immunotherapy in the first line setting commonly respond to treatments yet the majority develop resistance. A minority of patients will present with primary resistance to immunotherapy, making predicting patients’ response to immunotherapy a critical milestone in deciding appropriate treatment plans given the expanding list of options available. Hemoxylin and Eosin (H&E) images are frequently obtained through clinical care and contain spatial and morphological characteristics beyond cancer diagnosis. title: CollaBot: a RAG-based conversational agent system for supporting collaborative learning
abstract: This study focuses on collaborative learning scenarios and, based on scaffolding strategies for small groups proposed by educational experts, applies cutting-edge AI technologies such as generative AI and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to design and develop a conversational agent system named Col-laBot. The system could provide personalized metacognitive, cognitive, and social scaffolding to collaborative groups based on multiple sources of data, including writing behaviors, writing content, and group discussion discourse, during the collaborative learning process. A randomized controlled experiment study was conducted with 42 students, where the control group used a traditional task script, while the experimental group used CollaBot for collaborative learning. The study investigated students' learning performance, co-regulation strategies use and their perceptions of CollaBot. The results showed that Col-laBot significantly improved students’ learning performance and was perceived as particularly supportive in task planning, time management, and peer interaction, although its effect on co-regulation strategies use was not significant. This study provides valuable insights into the design and development of conversational systems for facilitating collaborative learning.

title: mcp-fdsnws-event: An MCP gateway for FDSNWS-event web services
abstract: Earthquake catalogues and event metadata are essential for monitoring seismic activity, consulting event lists and bulletins, and supporting both operational and research workflows. Access to these resources, however, still typically assumes users who can address FDSNWS-Event endpoints directly and interpret tabular or QuakeML responses programmatically. This creates a practical obstacle as conversational interfaces and agent-based systems are increasingly used for earthquake-related tasks, while requiring tools that are discoverable, schema-driven, and easy to reuse across multiple interaction turns. mcp-fdsnws-event addresses this interoperability problem by exposing FDSNWS-Event web services as structured Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools. The server provides six read-only tools covering event search, single-event detail, arrivals, magnitudes, origins, and focal mechanisms. Its implementation combines two access paths: compact catalogue queries are executed through the FDSNWS-Event format=text interface, while event detail is retrieved as QuakeML and serialized through ObsPy. The software supports multiple FDSN-compliant datacenters through a single parameterized interface, ships as a Docker container, and optionally exposes the same MCP tools through an OpenAPI/REST wrapper for web clients. Every tool is exercised against the four advertised providers, and the resulting conformance matrix documents where a provider does not implement an optional FDSNWS-Event subresource, so coverage is reported rather than assumed; each case is additionally mirrored by a response captured from that service, keeping the evidence reproducible without network access. The resulting software provides a standardized bridge between established seismological web services and the emerging ecosystem of MCP-enabled AI applications.

title: SwinGTANet: A federated temporal–graph intelligence framework for explainable anomaly detection in hybrid aerial–underwater drone networks
abstract: Hybrid aerial–aquatic ecosystems integrating Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) with underwater drones are increasingly critical for maritime monitoring, coastal security, and environmental intelligence. However, reliable anomaly detection in such systems remains challenging due to dynamic operating conditions, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) multimodal data, accessibility constraints for operators with disabilities, and strict communication and privacy limitations. These factors significantly restrict the applicability of conventional centralized and unimodal approaches in real-world deployments. To address these challenges, this study proposes SwinGTANet, a federated and explainable anomaly detection framework tailored for hybrid UAV–underwater networks. The framework incorporates Multi-Scale Adaptive Signal Decomposition (MASD) for noise-resilient preprocessing and Statistical–Spectral–Graph Embedding with Entropy-Guided Balancing (SSGE-EGB) for compact and discriminative feature representation. The core model integrates Swin-based temporal attention, graph convolutional reasoning, and temporal convolutional modeling, while a neurosymbolic fusion layer enhances interpretability and operational trust. Extensive experiments on a real-world multimodal dataset demonstrate that SwinGTANet achieves 98.6% accuracy, 99.1% AUC, and 96.7% temporal consistency, while maintaining robustness under severe channel impairments, data sparsity, and federated non-IID conditions. With an inference latency of 1.56 ms per sample, the framework ensures real-time performance with reduced communication overhead. These results highlight the practical significance of SwinGTANet in enabling scalable, privacy-preserving, and interpretable anomaly detection, supporting reliable deployment of intelligent UAV–underwater systems in safety-critical maritime environments.

title: ExecRetrieval: Measuring the Functional-Correctness Gap in Code-Embedding Retrieval
abstract: Embedding-based code retrieval is a core component of coding agents and retrieval-augmented code generation, where retrieving correct code matters more than retrieving lexically similar code. Existing code-retrieval benchmarks do not plant controlled, execution-verified single-edit variants of each query's canonical implementation in the search pool, leaving the question of whether embeddings can functionally discriminate correct from near-clone-but-incorrect code unanswered in a retrieval setting. Resolving this requires a benchmark whose search pool itself contains the relevant counterfactuals -- execution-verified buggy variants near-identical to each canonical -- so that a retriever's rank ordering can be directly tested for functional discrimination rather than topical or identity overlap. We introduce ExecRetrieval, 939 Python tasks each paired with one execution-verified canonical implementation and up to four execution-verified buggy distractors, each generated by a mechanical mutation making a single targeted edit, and evaluate 23 dense embedding configurations plus BM25 under provider-native invocation with paired McNemar tests and query-level bootstrap intervals. With near-clone counterfactuals in the pool, the top hosted system reaches exec@10 = 1.00 but only exec@1 = 0.331; rank-1 misses are paired buggy variants 91.5-99.4% of the time across the four leading systems, and the canonical scores below at least one of its four paired distractors in 67-78% of queries on the leading systems. The full dataset, execution oracle, embedding matrices, environment snapshot, and pairwise statistical tests are released at the URL in Appendix D.

title: Classic AI Scaffolding for LLM Social Agents
abstract: Large language models can produce locally plausible social turns, but fluent next-turn generation is not enough for social simulation. Human encounters such as restaurant lunches and hotel check-ins are bounded social episodes with roles, scripts, material state, obligations, commitments, timing, and closure conditions. We present EpisodeSim, a hybrid LLM-agent architecture that represents classic-AI structures as natural-language control state interpreted by LLM calls. A World Master maintains shared reality, constructs scenes, adjudicates proposed actions, tracks effects and obligations, and controls closure. Experiments with small qualitative ablations on two held-out settings support a design claim: LLM fluency supplies local texture, but coherent social simulation benefits from persistent classic-AI-style scaffolding that organizes behavior over time.

title: Flow Reasoning Models: Turning Flows Into Efficient Recurrent Reasoners
abstract: Structured reasoning requires making and revising interdependent decisions to reach a globally consistent solution. Existing architectures struggle with this: autoregressive models commit sequentially and cannot revise earlier decisions, while masked diffusion models often require careful decoding schemes to coordinate interdependent predictions. We introduce Flow Reasoning Models (FRMs), a novel framework for structured reasoning that adapts continuous flows over discrete structured outputs with a simple recurrent refinement mechanism. By self-conditioning a flow model on its own past outputs, we turn one-shot denoising into iterative solution refinement. This lets FRMs make and revise decisions in parallel, efficiently coordinating interdependent choices across solutions. Yet conventional self-conditioning becomes unreliable at greater recurrent depth due to exposure bias between one-step training predictions and recursively generated inference states. We address this mismatch with Fixed-Point Forcing (FPF), which trains FRMs on states produced by their own inference dynamics while preserving the standard flow-matching objective. FRMs achieve solve rates of 99.5%, 100.0%, and 99.9% on Sudoku-Extreme, Zebra, and Maze-Unique, respectively. On Sudoku-Extreme, FRMs achieve higher peak accuracy than the evaluated masked-diffusion and specialized reasoning baselines while remaining highly compute-efficient, matching the next-best method's 98.7% peak solve rate with 44times fewer inference FLOPs.

title: Compile‐Once Block Encodings for Masked Similarity‐Transformed Effective Hamiltonians
abstract: ABSTRACT We present COMPOSER, a compile‐once modular parametric oracle for similarity‐encoded effective reduction of electronic‐structure operators (e.g., Schrieffer–Wolff‐type constructions). Low‐rank factorizations compress Hamiltonians into empirically near‐linear ladder pools at fixed factorization thresholds, and represent anti‐Hermitian generators through threshold‐controlled bilinear, decomposable‐pair, or generic elementary‐excitation branch libraries; each declared primitive branch admits a number‐conserving Fock‐space block encoding, with coefficient‐space dyads understood through their number‐conserving second‐quantized lifts. A fixed PREP‐SELECT‐PREP template multiplexes these branches, and a standard block‐Hamiltonian simulation/QSP primitive exponentiates the Hermitian generator with degree or query complexity set by operator norms and the chosen error tolerance. For a fixed orbital pool, qubit register, branch‐primitive library, selector address map, ancilla layout, routing plan, maximum branch set, and global normalization, the two‐qubit fabric is compiled once; geometry, active‐space (mask) updates, and truncations are absorbed by updated numerical weights, rotation angles, and classical masks. We introduce a mask‐aware similarity‐sandwich effective‐Hamiltonian construction and benchmark stability under low‐rank and second‐order‐perturbation‐guided screening. COMPOSER is an execution architecture: algorithmic errors (block‐encoding and QSP approximation) are tunable for any supplied parameters, while physical accuracy depends on how those parameters are obtained if not refined.

title: Signs, Transparency, and Semantic Paradoxes
abstract: The principle of (semiotic) transparency—associated with Husserl and discussed extensively in Polish logical semiotics (Ossowski, Koj)—says, roughly, that when an object functions for a subject as a sign of something, the sign itself becomes “transparent” to certain cognitive operations. Leon Koj proposed an axiomatic articulation of this idea and argued that it yields a general prohibition on semantic self-reference sufficient to block semantic antinomies. This paper has two aims. First, it reconstructs Koj’s explication and clarifies what sort of transparency it requires (and what it does not). Second, it argues that Koj’s principle, understood as he needs it for paradox-blocking, cannot be accepted: it is both too strong as a claim about sign-use and too weak as a general strategy against semantic paradoxes. The paper’s upshot is that the principle is better understood as describing a family of pragmatic and attentional constraints on certain uses of expressions, rather than as underwriting a universal prohibition on semantic self-reference.

title: Where Perceptrons Meet Proof Trees: A Critical Survey Review of Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of neuro-symbolic and reasoning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Self-Correcting Digital Circuits Based on Reservoir Computing
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to digital circuit design centered around reservoir computing and self-correction mechanisms. Traditional digital circuit design methodologies often grapple with the detrimental effects of inherent noise and process variations, leading to unreliable and inconsistent performance. The core idea is to leverage the dynamic adaptation properties of reservoir computing, specifically recurrent neural networks, to create circuits that actively mitigate the impact of noise. The proposed architecture utilizes a digital circuit implementation of a reservoir, allowing for real-time adjustment of its parameters to compensate for disturbances. Mathematical formulations detail the dynamics of the reservoir and the control signals necessary for self-correction. The resulting circuits exhibit enhanced robustness and improved performance in the presence of noise, marking a significant step towards more reliable and adaptable digital hardware. This work demonstrates a viable pathway to building inherently self-correcting digital circuits, addressing a critical limitation in current digital design practices. ---

title: Composable Neural Modules with Formal Interface Specifications
abstract: The construction of complex neural networks from individual modules frequently relies on intuitive design choices, resulting in a lack of formal guarantees regarding their composability. This paper proposes a novel framework for designing modular neural networks based on formal interface specifications. We introduce a dedicated language to precisely define the inputs, outputs, and functional behavior of neural modules, allowing for automated verification of compatibility and ensuring seamless integration during network construction. This approach shifts the focus from ad-hoc design to a rigorous, verifiable methodology, promoting reusability, reducing integration complexity, and ultimately contributing to the development of more robust and reliable neural network architectures. The core of this work lies in establishing a mathematically sound foundation for modular neural network design, addressing a critical limitation in current practices. We outline a formal system with a focus on ensuring correct composition and enabling automated verification, ultimately leading to more trustworthy and maintainable AI systems. ---

title: Bogota Tapeti: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bogota Tapeti Bird
abstract: This paper presents Bogota Tapeti, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bogota Tapeti bird ( *Thraupis episcopus* ). The algorithm leverages the tapeti's unique strategy of searching for food in a patch-based manner, combined with a novel adaptive mutation operator. Bogota Tapeti aims to improve upon existing metaheuristic techniques, particularly in addressing premature convergence and enhancing exploration capabilities. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a patch-based representation and dynamically adjusting the size and distribution of patches based on the algorithm's progress. The core of the algorithm lies in its adaptive mutation operator, which probabilistically modifies the patch assignment and food quantity within each patch, promoting diversity and preventing stagnation. We evaluate Bogota Tapeti on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA). The experimental results show that Bogota Tapeti exhibits strong convergence rates and robustness across a range of problem types. Future work will focus on refining the adaptive mutation operator and exploring potential applications of the algorithm in areas such as machine learning and engineering design.

authors: Regina Aparecida Prisco Paiva Garcia Silva

abstract: Knowledge Organization Systems (KOSs) are instruments used to organize, represent and retrieve information and knowledge. This study presents an experience report on the integrated construction of four KOSs: taxonomy, classification system, thesaurus and ontology, supported by a glossary and a concept map. The objective was to report on the practical experience of developing these instruments and to understand the relationships established among them. The research is characterized as qualitative, applied, descriptive and exploratory, focusing on information search and retrieval systems as its domain. The process involved selecting and analyzing a text representative of the domain, identifying and selecting concepts, and constructing the instruments using the Cmap, Thesa and Protégé software. The results revealed distinct structures, semantic relationships and levels of formalization among the instruments, while demonstrating that their articulated construction allows each stage to support subsequent ones. Difficulties were also identified in defining conceptual relationships and using the technological tools, particularly in the development of the concept map and ontology. It is concluded that the integrated construction of KOSs contributed to both the theoretical and practical understanding of their characteristics and relationships, highlighting their pedagogical potential for teaching and learning Knowledge Organization.

title: Determining the Minimum Amount of Tissue Required for Outcome-Relevant Histopathologic Feature Stratification in NMIBC
abstract: Background - Non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) comprises 75% of bladder cancer diagnoses and is characterized by frequent recurrence. Clinical management is guided by risk stratification, which incorporates subjectively assessed tumour grade. Digital pathology enables objective quantification of features from whole slide images (WSIs), however the minimum cancer tissue needed for reliable grading is undefined, and the prognostic significance of small high-grade components in otherwise low-grade cancers remains uncertain. We hypothesize that there exists a minimum number of cancer cells sufficient to capture clinically relevant histopathologic features such as recurrence-free survival. Methods - The cohort included a single digitized WSI from each of 163 patients with stage Ta NMIBC and clinical follow-up data. Quantitative measurements of 11 nuclear features were extracted from each WSI using digital pathology software (Visiopharm, Hørsholm, Denmark). Each WSI was sampled into progressively smaller tissue subsets. At each sampling threshold, Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence assessed similarity in feature distributions relative to the full WSI. Nuclear features were then summarized at each sampling threshold and used to stratify patients for Kaplan-Meier analysis of their association with recurrence-free survival. Results - We found feature distributions showed the greatest improvement in similarity to the full slide between 5% and 25% tissue sampling, with only smaller gains as more tissue was added. Lesser nuclear diameter and eccentricity retained prognostic significance with limited sampling, whereas ellipticalness, solidity, and convexity were relatively more sensitive to limited sampling. Survival analyses found higher sampling thresholds recovered more significant prognostic features, with thresholds of 20-25% showing feature recovery most comparable to full-slide analysis. Conclusions - This study begins to establish quantitative tissue thresholds for digital pathology in NMIBC. These findings may improve the efficiency and standardization of computational pathology and help define specimen adequacy thresholds.Faculty Supervisors: Dr. Steven Smith, Dr. Nicholas Held

title: Toward a Semantic Framework for Classical Chinese Poetry: Multilingual and Decentralized Integration of East Asian Literary Heritage
abstract: Classical Chinese poetry, a classical form composed in Literary Chinese, originated in China and spread across East Asia, including Japan, Korea, and Vietnam. It has played a key role in elite education, cultural diplomacy, and political communication. Despite its cultural significance, research on its semantic modeling remains limited, and digital representations often face issues like fragmentation and structural inconsistencies. This paper proposes a decentralized semantic infrastructure for Classical Chinese poetry as a multilingual resource for cultural heritage. The system is organized into three layers: (i) multilingual SKOS vocabularies to represent poetic concepts; (ii) OWL ontologies that reuse BIBFRAME for bibliographic structure and FOAF for authorship representation; and (iii) a distributed RDF resource layer supporting SPARQL 1.1 federated queries across poetic corpora. The infrastructure implements TEI standards for structuring poetic materials, including metadata and digitized text, while reserving interfaces for potential IIIF integration. Future work will focus on expanding multilingual vocabularies and integrating with cultural heritage platforms.

title: Automated signal-to-noise ratio-based optimization of traveling-wave parametric amplifiers for multiplexed qubit readout
abstract: Scaling superconducting quantum processors to hundreds of qubits requires frequency-multiplexed readout architectures, where the non-uniform gain profile of Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers (TWPAs) creates a critical bottleneck. We present an automated optimization framework that addresses the weakest link problem in multiplexed readout by employing a geometric mean cost function to maintain a uniform signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) profile across all channels. Through systematic characterization of a 5-qubit system, we demonstrate that readout fidelity saturates above SNR ≈ 2.5, indicating that in the high-performance regime SNR is a more effective optimization metric for TWPAs than readout fidelity. Our optimization framework, based on the Nelder-Mead simplex algorithm with continuous parameter tuning, reaches the optimized operating point in ∼100 measurements, reducing the search effort by a factor of 4.5 compared to a 451-point exhaustive grid method. Notably, the continuous optimization surpasses the grid search maximum by 12.8% in geometric mean SNR, confirming its superior efficiency over conventional grid search methods. This automated approach provides a scalable solution for maintaining a uniformly high level of readout fidelity across various amplifier devices in large-scale quantum processors.

title: A Distributed Quantum Blind Millionaire Protocol Based on Quantum Walks
abstract: ABSTRACT The quantum blind millionaire (QBM) problem is a fundamental primitive in quantum secure multi‐party computation. It enables two groups to compare aggregated private sums while protecting individual data, and is widely adopted in privacy‐preserving collaborative decision‐making. However, most existing QBM protocols either rely on semi‐honest third parties or adopt sophisticated quantum states. These approaches lead to high resource overhead and operational complexity, which restricts practical deployment. In this paper, we apply the one‐directional quantum walks on a circle (ODQWC) to the QBM problem for the first time and develop a new distributed QBM protocol. This scheme employs only a single quantum walker and requires no trusted third party. Moreover, the proposed protocol achieves higher qubit efficiency than most existing mainstream QBM protocols, with an efficiency exceeding . According to our analysis, the protocol passes the verification of both correctness and security, and its feasibility is confirmed via IBM Qiskit simulations. The proposed scheme solves the QBM problem efficiently and can serve as a building block for broader multi‐party collaborative computation tasks.

title: The Memory Trust Gap: Capability-Dependent Failures in Persistent-Memory Agents
abstract: Persistent memory supports personalized agents, but a stale stored fact can override current authoritative evidence without warning. We study when this harm begins as model capability changes. We evaluate a frozen, closed-set, action-scored benchmark with 2 suites that represent 2 different meanings of "no memory" (a Benefit suite, unsolvable without the stored fact, and a Safety suite, in which an authoritative tool always holds the correct value), on a same-family model-size series (Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B). The Memory Trust Gap reflects over-trust rather than confusion. In the Benefit suite, models answer with the stale value 0.92-1.00 of the time at every scale. In the Safety suite, harm below the no-memory baseline under the trap conditions ($Δ_{\mathrm{mem}}$) is capability-gated, with the larger models collapsing most once a stale note is made to look current. In a $2\times2\times2\times2$ factorial, which feature triggers over-trust depends on both the feature and model scale. Removing a label amplifies over-trust at every size, and a recency feature (stale dated newer) fools the larger models harder. Source authority is weak and scale-flat, and position changes from positive to negative across the Qwen3 model-size series. We confirm these scale interactions with direct cross-size contrast tests rather than overlapping per-model intervals. Mitigation is likewise capability-dependent: exposing metadata improves accuracy for the capable models, but only pre-resolving the conflict restores accuracy for the 2 smaller checkpoints. The same pattern appears on the capable models in an independent Llama-Instruct model-size series and on 2 external datasets (RGB, MisBench). A framing control finds no consistent advantage for the memory label: at the 3 smaller scales, models trust a stale document more than a stale memory; at 8B, the difference is not significant.

title: Measuring Optimal Transport in Transformer Depth
abstract: A transformer carries each token's state from layer to layer, and the whole vocabulary carried together forms a cloud that moves with depth. We ask whether a trained network moves this cloud the way optimal transport would: at the cheapest cost, and along the map that pairs each token with its optimal destination. We measure both on Pythia-160m and Pythia-410m, with an exact assignment between consecutive layer clouds, a measured sampling floor, calibration on couplings known to be optimal, and a split of the cost into the common shift of the cloud and the token-specific moves. At the last layer, both models move their tokens where the optimal-transport map sends them, at the optimal cost for Pythia-410m and slightly above it for Pythia-160m. At the first layer they do not. In between, single layers can be judged on cost at only two of ten transitions, and blocks of several layers move the cloud at close to the optimal cost. The agreement at the last layer is much weaker at initialisation (0.64 against 0.86) and grows with training.

title: Solutions to Three Conjectures and an Open Problem on Binary BCH Codes
abstract: BCH codes are among the most important classes of cyclic codes and have played a central role in coding theory and its applications. One of the fundamental problems in the study of BCH codes is to determine their exact minimum distances, which directly govern their error-correcting capability. Although the BCH bound provides a general lower bound, determining the exact minimum distance is often difficult, and many parameter families remain unresolved. In this paper, we investigate three conjectures and an open problem on binary BCH codes proposed by Chen, Xie, and Ding in \cite{Chen59}. We settle these conjectures on the exact minimum distances of three families of binary BCH codes by constructing codewords attaining the BCH bound. Beyond these conjectures, we further study the more difficult family codes and determine its minimum distance for some cases. We further study Open Problem 8.4: affirmative answers are obtained for the first two length families, while for the third family a sufficient condition is established and a counterexample shows that the unrestricted assertion does not hold in general.

title: EchoSonar-R: A Multi-View Reasoning-Enabled Model for Disease Classification and Report Generation in Echocardiography
abstract: Echocardiography is the most widely used non-invasive cardiac imaging modality, providing essential information for cardiovascular diagnosis. Interpreting an echocardiogram requires synthesizing complementary evidence across multiple heart views to identify abnormalities and produce structured clinical reports. While recent efforts focus on improving classification performance, most models lack explicit diagnostic reasoning and spatially grounded anatomical evidence, limiting clinician trust. We present EchoSonar-R, a multi-view reasoning-enabled vision-language model that jointly performs multi-label disease classification and report generation from echocardiography studies. EchoSonar-R combines a spatiotemporal video encoder with a structure-aware cardiac detector that provides spatially grounded anatomical cues to improve interpretability and clinician trust during cross-view reasoning. EchoSonar-R is trained in two stages: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on reasoning-annotated targets, followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task-specific rewards that jointly align classification and report generation within a unified reinforcement-learning framework. Across a private multi-view dataset and two public benchmarks, EchoSonar-R improves macro balanced accuracy by 17.1% on the private set and 6.1% on MIMICEchoQA over the strongest baseline, achieves a GREEN clinical faithfulness score of 0.800, and produces interpretable reasoning traces grounded in multi-view visual evidence.

title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Hybrid Embeddings for Smarter Chatbots
abstract: The rapid evolution of conversational AI systems has transformed from rule-based interactions to sophisticated naturallanguage processing capabilities. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) represents a paradigmatic shift by combiningthe strengths of information retrieval systems with generative language models, enabling chatbots to produce factuallygrounded responses. However, traditional RAG implementations face significant limitations due to their reliance on eitherdense embeddings or sparse embeddings exclusively. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into enhancingRAG systems through hybrid embeddings that synergistically combine dense semantic representations with sparse lexicalfeatures. Our proposed HybridRAG architecture demonstrates superior performance in retrieval accuracy, responsequality, and contextual understanding across multiple domains including healthcare, customer support, and education.Experimental results show improvements of 18% in faithfulness scores, 23% in answer relevance, and 15% in overalluser satisfaction compared to traditional RAG approaches. The integration of transformer-based dense embeddings withBM25-based sparse representations enables more robust information retrieval while maintaining computationalefficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of conversational AI by providing a scalable framework fordeveloping context-aware, factually accurate chatbot systems.

title: Ontology-driven construction and governance of multimodal datasets for telecommunications
abstract: To address insufficient domain knowledge representation, cross-modal semantic mismatches, and the absence of closed-loop quality governance in multimodal dataset construction for the telecommunications industry, an ontology-driven construction and governance framework, OntoDataset, was proposed. A three-layer architecture for knowledge modeling, semantic reasoning, and data generation was established with a domain ontology as the unified semantic foundation. An ontology-guided algorithm, OntAlign, was also designed to align multimodal data by integrating entity, relation, and contextual constraints. Experiments on real business data from a large telecommunications operator showed that, compared with the best-performing baseline, overall data quality was improved from 86.7% to 93.0%, annotation efficiency was increased from 250 to 455 samples per hour, and the manual intervention rate was reduced from 18% to 12%. In downstream-task evaluations, the AUC for customer churn prediction was 0.897, while the macroaveraged F1 score and accuracy for customer intent recognition were 0.856 and 0.873, respectively. The results indicate that the proposed method improves the quality, consistency, and construction efficiency of multimodal datasets in vertical industries and provides technical support for dataset construction and continuous governance for industry-oriented large models.

title: Semantic Orchestration for Time-Domain Astronomy
abstract: Time-domain astronomy relies on heterogeneous data from telescopes, surveys, detectors, archives, and value-added alert brokers. Those instruments may capture the same astronomical phenomena, yet their data interfaces and response structures differ, as do their identifiers and semantic conventions. We present Alertissimo, a research prototype for the semantic orchestration of heterogeneous astronomical data services. At its core, a hierarchical semantic model assigns provider-neutral, serialization-independent addresses to astronomical entities, measurements, classifications, associations, and data products. Reusable concepts are composed into typed records whose context distinguishes the role of each value, while provenance and explicit relationships between records are preserved in canonical, object-centric Portfolios. Alertissimo supports provider-agnostic scientific workflows that are expressed through a domain-specific language (DSL) and compiled into a typed intermediate representation independent of any particular broker or service. The principal contribution is an executable semantic layer that decouples scientific intent from provider interfaces without depending on the universal adoption of a single standard or serialization. It also provides a deterministic target for future natural-language interfaces: a language model may translate user requests into the DSL.

title: Code to perform non-pararmetric supervised learning with Gaussian Process, the correlation function of which is parametrised by a non-parametric kernel, leading to a non-stationary GP.
abstract: Code to implement a new supervised learning method, the input-out relationship is modelled as a sample function of a Gaussian Process, the correlation function of which kernel parametrised. The hard-to-implement explicitly non-stationary kernel with input-pair dependent hyperparameters, is replaced by a parsimonious input-specific ARD kernel in which each hyperparameter is a (GP-generated) random function computed at each iteration of the (MCMC-based) inference. Information obtained from inter-comparison of interloping lookback windows, is used to learn all relevant parameters. The small second code is for matrix inversion. The third code on this site performs an learning of the lengthscale hyperparameters of an ARD kernel that parametrises the correlation function of the GP that models the relation between the energy consumption variable, and four meteorological parameters, using SVGP, given the training data is a subset of the Tetouan city data. Predictions at the test inputs then follow. The last code on this site performs learning+prediction on these training and test sets with DNNs.

title: An AI-Driven Framework For Predictive Customer Experience And Personalized Digital Marketing: An Empirical Study with Special Reference to Coimbatore District, Tamil Nadu
abstract: This study develops and empirically examines an AI-driven framework for predictive customer experience (PCX) and personalized digital marketing (PDM), with special reference to consumers in Coimbatore District, Tamil Nadu.The framework integrates AI-enabled predictive analytics, recommendation systems, conversational AI, customer-data integration, personalization quality, perceived usefulness, trust, privacy concern, customer engagement, satisfaction, and purchase intention.A quantitative, cross-sectional research design is proposed using a structured questionnaire administered to digitally active consumers in Coimbatore District.The study recommends a sample of 400 respondents and the use of descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation, multiple regression, and structural equation modelling (SEM) to test the proposed relationships.The framework assumes that AI capability improves personalization quality and predictive relevance, which in turn enhance customer experience and engagement; however, privacy concerns are expected to weaken the positive effect when customers perceive excessive surveillance or insufficient control over personal data.The article contributes a locally contextualized model for businesses, marketers, and researchers seeking to implement responsible AI-driven marketing.Because this manuscript is designed as a research-ready article, numerical findings are not fabricated; the Results section provides a statistical reporting template to be completed after primary-data collection.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED AUTOMATIC EVALUATION SYSTEMS: APPROACHES TO ASSESSING THE QUALITY OF WRITTEN AND INTERPRETING TRANSLATION, RELIABILITY, AND APPLICATION PERSPECTIVES
abstract: Purpose of this study is to analyze the role of artificial intelligence-based automatic evaluation systems in assessing the quality of written and interpreting translation, as well as to examine their methodological foundations and reliability. Design/method/approach is based on comparative and analytical methods combined with a systematic review of existing scientific literature. The study covers both traditional and neural evaluation metrics such as BLEU, METEOR, TER, BERTScore, and COMET, as well as large language model (LLM)-based evaluation approaches. Findings (Results) indicate that AI-based systems have strong potential in translation quality assessment; however, they still cannot fully replace human expertise, particularly in interpreting, where multimodal factors play a critical role.

title: DSAP Bench: Evaluating Safety Boundary Erosion in Large Language Models using Domain-Specific Adversarial Prompts
abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) in professional and decision-support are increasing in scale. This integration rise a concern in their ability to maintain safety boundaries when responding to adversarial prompts which are crafted like a professional query. Jailbreak benchmarks and studies are generally oriented to explicit harmful or sensitive text, which is not necessarily a reasonable reflection of the misuse cases in the real world, where adversarial intent is hidden in the form of legitimate professional reuse. To mitigate this shortcoming, the present paper presents a Domain-Specific Adversarial Prompt (DSAP) dataset of 4,240 prompts aimed at testing safety boundaries of LLMs focusing integration in domain such as finance, medicine, law, media, and cybersecurity. Besides the dataset, we suggest the structured safety assessment scheme based on the two complementary scoring schemes, namely the Prompt Aggressiveness Score (PAS) and the Universal Safety Boundary Erosion Rating (USBER). Based on these scores, several calculated safety metrics are obtained, such as Refusal rate, Drift rate, Attack Success rate (ASR) and Domain Vulnerability Index (DVI) which can allow a cross-domain comparison of safety behaviour in a systematic manner. It was empirically evaluated on 300 adversarial prompts per domain in which responses generated by a large language model were evaluated using automated scoring. The findings demonstrate significant differences in domain-specific safety behaviour. The medical domain demonstrates the lowest explicit harmful responses with the lowest Attack Success Rate, though it exhibits the highest drift rate through extensive contextual engagement and the lowest refusal rate. The law domain shows the lowest overall vulnerability as measured by the Domain Vulnerability Index, with moderate drift and explicit failures. In contrast, the finance domain emerges with the highest Attack Success Rate, indicating substantial susceptibility to adversarial prompts in professional financial advisory settings. Domains involving narrative framing or technical reasoning, particularly media and cybersecurity, exhibit the highest levels of safety boundary erosion. The cybersecurity domain demonstrates the highest Domain Vulnerability Index among all evaluated domains, while the media domain also shows significant vulnerability. These results suggest that the contextual framing of prompts plays a very important role in the way the models interpret and react to potentially unsafe requests. The data structure and assessment model suggested would offer a well-organised and scholarly suitable standard by which the behaviour of safety boundaries will be examined in domain-specific settings. The present work emphasizes the significance of domain-sensitive safety assessment and provides novel information regarding the weaknesses of contemporary language models by concentrating on indirect adversarial prompts in the context of realistic professional settings.

title: Zero-Knowledge Governance: Cryptographic Compliance Auditing for Federated Edge AI
abstract: The rapid expansion of Federated Learning (FL) within Edge AI has enabled decentralized networks to collaboratively train sophisticated models without sharing raw, privacy-sensitive data [8]. However, this strict adherence to data privacy creates a significant "blind spot" for AI governance. Under emerging regulatory frameworks like the EU AI Act, regulators require proof of data safety, bias mitigation, and privacy preservation [4]. The current paradigm forces a paradox: regulators cannot verify whether individual edge nodes complied with these laws without violating the very privacy FL is designed to protect. In this paper, we propose a novel Zero-Knowledge Governance (ZKG) framework. By integrating Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments of Knowledge (zk-SNARKs) into the local edge training phase, edge devices can cryptographically prove that their local datasets and model updates comply with encoded governance policies, without ever revealing the underlying data [1]. We present the architectural design of ZKG, analyze the vulnerabilities it addresses in decentralized AI, and propose optimizations to make cryptographic auditing viable for resource-constrained edge hardware.

title: ## Canyon Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Canyon Mouse Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Canyon Mouse, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of canyon mice. Canyon mice exhibit a fascinating strategy of navigating complex terrain to locate food sources, utilizing subtle changes in elevation and visual cues. This behavior has been translated into a novel algorithm designed for solving complex optimization problems. Canyon Mouse employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), with a unique "canyon exploration" mechanism to promote efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space. The algorithm operates within a multi-dimensional space, representing the optimization variables. The core mechanism involves maintaining a population of candidate solutions (particles) and iteratively adjusting their positions and velocities based on environmental factors – simulated canyon topography and visual perception. The algorithm utilizes a self-adaptive learning rate mechanism and a novel "canyon shift" operator to dynamically adjust the search direction. Experimental results, presented in detail in Section 3, demonstrate Canyon Mouse's effectiveness across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance and adaptability. The algorithm's design emphasizes robust exploration, efficient convergence, and adaptability to different problem landscapes. Keywords: Metaheuristic, Particle Swarm Optimization, Simulated Annealing, Canyon Mouse, Optimization Algorithm, Exploration, Exploitation. ---

title: Spectral Graph-Based Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning using spectral graphs. Traditional knowledge representation methods often struggle with complex relationships and dependencies, particularly in domains with intricate interconnections. We introduce the concept of representing knowledge as a spectral graph, where nodes represent entities and edges represent relationships, and the graph's spectral properties encode the relationships. This approach leverages the inherent structure within the graph, enabling efficient reasoning and querying through spectral algorithms. We demonstrate the potential of this method to handle complex knowledge structures and improve the accuracy and efficiency of inference tasks. The core claim of this work is that utilizing spectral graphs allows for a more robust and effective representation and reasoning process compared to conventional methods. The key mechanism involves the application of spectral graph algorithms for knowledge inference. This research expands the theoretical foundation for knowledge representation and provides a new paradigm for intelligent systems. ---

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Topology for Data Compression (NETD)
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Euclidean Topology (NETD), a novel approach to data compression based on the principles of non-Euclidean topology. Traditional compression algorithms often rely on the inherent properties of Euclidean geometry, limiting their effectiveness with large datasets. NETD leverages the inherent structure of data represented as graphs, constructing a graph-based representation where topology plays a crucial role in data compression efficiency. This paper explores the mathematical foundations of NETD, detailing the construction process and demonstrating its potential for superior compression rates compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around the inherent structure of data, allowing for a more efficient representation and reduced storage requirements.

title: Dimensional Convergence and Nonlinear Geometry Structures
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic dimensional aggregation and adaptive geometric structures to numerical simulations, focusing on the modeling of complex physical phenomena, particularly high-dimensional quantum entanglement. We introduce a novel 'Dimensional Aggregator' module, which dynamically decomposes spatial dimensions and employs self-adaptive geometric transformations to reconstruct the resulting space. The core mechanism lies in the dynamic creation of geometric structures, rather than static transformations, enabling a more nuanced and potentially more accurate representation of the underlying physics. This approach offers a new pathway to simulate complex systems exhibiting non-linear geometry and offers enhanced precision compared to traditional methods. The paper details the implementation of the Dimensional Aggregator, explores its impact on simulation fidelity, and discusses the potential for future research extending this methodology to broader applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement Modeling in Neural Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance the accuracy of neural simulations, particularly within complex neural networks. The core claim posits that leveraging quantum entanglement can provide a novel approach to modeling neuronal behavior, moving beyond traditional simulation methods. The proposed mechanism involves mapping synaptic connections within neurons to quantum bits (Qubits) and utilizing entanglement to perform parallel computations across multiple synaptic connections. Quantum measurements are then employed to simulate the probabilistic nature of neuronal firing. This research explores a fundamental shift – directly applying quantum mechanical principles to neural simulation rather than treating them as mere heuristic optimization tools. The theoretical framework developed presents a pathway for exploring the impact of quantum effects on neural processing and potentially leading to more accurate and efficient models of biological neural networks. This work lays the groundwork for future investigations into the quantum computational properties of the brain.

title: Teaching the Colossus to Say No: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of alignment and large language models as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Blyth's Vole: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Myodes blythii*
abstract: This paper presents Blyth's Vole, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Myodes blythii* (Blyth's vole), a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptable foraging strategies. The algorithm combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation mechanism mimicking the vole's behavioral patterns. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a 'memory' component, analogous to the vole's caching behavior, to enhance the search process. The core of Blyth's Vole lies in its dynamically adjusted parameters, influenced by the local landscape and historical search data, resulting in improved convergence and robustness. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities. The key features of Blyth's Vole include a dynamically adjusted inertia weight in PSO, a temperature schedule informed by the local search history, and a caching mechanism for promising solutions. The results suggest that this algorithm represents a significant contribution to the field of metaheuristic optimization, particularly for problems exhibiting complex landscapes and requiring adaptive search strategies. The performance metrics used for evaluation include solution quality (objective function value), convergence speed, and computational complexity.
